test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The reference date for the census 2027 for the Union Territory of Ladakh shall be _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1st day of October 2026**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reference date for the **Census 2027** specifically for the **Union Territory of Ladakh** has been designated as the **1st day of October 2026**.
 
• In the context of the Indian Census, the **reference date** is the specific moment in time to which the census data refers, ensuring that the population count is a "snapshot" of the country at that exact instance.
 
• For most parts of India, the census reference date is typically the **1st of March** of the census year. However, for **snow-bound areas** and high-altitude regions like **Ladakh**, the date is set earlier to facilitate enumeration before the onset of extreme winter conditions which make transportation and communication impossible.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs**, through the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, manages the scheduling and notification of these dates under the provisions of the **Census Act, 1948**.
 
• The choice of **October 1st** ensures that the administrative machinery can complete the head-counting process in the **Leh** and **Kargil** districts before heavy snowfall blocks the passes. ***Hence, the correct answer is 1st day of October 2026.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union Territory of Ladakh:**

 
 
• **Ladakh** was established as a **Union Territory** without a legislature on **October 31, 2019**, following the enactment of the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
 
• It is the **largest Union Territory** in India by area but has a very low population density due to its rugged mountainous terrain.
 
 
 
• **History of Census in India:**
 
 
• The first non-synchronous census in India was conducted in **1872** under **Lord Mayo**, while the first synchronous census took place in **1881**.
 
• Censuses are conducted every **10 years**. The **2021 Census** was significantly delayed due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**, leading to adjusted timelines for the subsequent data collection exercises.
 
 
 
• **Phases of Census:**
 
 
• A typical census is conducted in two phases: **House Listing & Housing Census** and **Population Enumeration**.
 
• For the upcoming cycle, the integration of **digital data collection** through mobile apps is a major technological feature designed to improve accuracy and speed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Framework:**

 
 
• The **Census Act of 1948** provides the legal backing for the census. It guarantees the **confidentiality** of the information provided by citizens, and the data can only be used for statistical purposes, not as evidence in a court of law.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Census Data:**
 
 
• The data is vital for the **Delimitation Commission** to fix the boundaries of **Parliamentary and Assembly constituencies** based on the latest population figures.
 
• It assists the government in identifying the socio-economic status of various groups to implement targeted welfare schemes and allocate **financial resources** under the guidance of the **Finance Commission**.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Authority:**
 
 
• The **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India** (RGCCI) is the nodal officer responsible for the execution of the census under the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**.
